title: AdapterSemanticProfile/v1
description: A typed semantic profile for a backend adapter: the contract between an SRL MathIR/v1 expression and a concrete computational backend (a solver, a CAS shim, a numeric kernel). The profile declares the subset of the MathIR allowlist it supports (supported_cds, each a '<cd>.<name>' drawn from MATH_IR_ALLOWLIST), how it behaves on each unsupported operator (unsupported_features: reject / approximate / drop), the input/output schema contracts, whether it is deterministic, its network posture, and its SPDX license. CRITICAL: supported_cds MUST be a subset of MATH_IR_ALLOWLIST; an op outside the allowlist fails profile validation (CONTRACT_INVALID) at the Python layer (srl.semantic.adapter_profiles.validate_profile). The profile carries the two safety consts (canonical_writes=0, grants_authority=false). Canonical JSON contract: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no NaN/Infinity, trailing newline.

profile_id.description: Content-addressed identity: sha256 over the canonical encoding of the profile (without this field), prefixed 'sha256:'. Computed by srl.semantic.adapter_profiles.profile_id.

adapter_id.description: Stable logical identifier of the backend adapter this profile describes (e.g. 'z3-smt-shim', 'numpy-linear-algebra'). Not a content hash; identity of a profile object is its profile_id.

pack_ref.description: An ArtifactRef/v1 pointing at the versioned, content-addressed adapter pack (the executable bytes this profile governs). Carried inline as a structural object (schema_version const ArtifactRef/v1, media_type, digest, size_bytes, optional path); the digest is authoritative, the path is a portable hint. The full ArtifactRef/v1 field contract (portable-path rejection etc.) is enforced at the Python layer by srl.semantic.adapter_profiles.validate_profile via validate_artifact_ref (the repo schema convention is inline structural shapes + python defense-in-depth, not cross-schema $ref, so validation works offline).

media_type.description: IANA-style media type of the referenced pack payload (e.g. application/vnd.srlab.adapter-pack+json).

digest.description: Content digest of the pack bytes: sha256 + 64 lowercase hex digits. The pack_hash a projection receipt binds is this digest.

size_bytes.description: Non-negative integer byte count of the referenced pack payload.

path.description: Optional portable repo-relative path to the pack bytes. Validated for portability at the Python layer (no '..', no drive letter, no leading '/', no backslash); the digest remains authoritative.

supported_cds.description: The subset of MATH_IR_ALLOWLIST this adapter accepts, each a '<cd>.<name>' pair. MUST be a subset of MATH_IR_ALLOWLIST; an entry outside it is rejected at profile-validation time (CONTRACT_INVALID). A subset (not the whole allowlist) is normal and expected: a solver need not support calculus1, for example. Empty is allowed only for a profile that rejects every operator (degenerate but well-formed).

unsupported_features.description: Per-operator behavior declarations for operators the profile does NOT support. Each entry names a 'feature' (a '<cd>.<name>' or a cd-level wildcard like 'calculus1.*') and the 'behavior' the adapter takes when the operator is encountered during projection: 'reject' (hard stop, IR_UNSUPPORTED), 'approximate' (recorded as a lossy assumption), or 'drop' (silently elided, recorded as a dropped feature). An operator present here should not also be in supported_cds (validated at the Python layer).

feature.description: The operator or operator-group the declaration covers: a '<cd>.<name>' pair or a cd-level wildcard '<cd>.*'.

behavior.description: The adapter behavior on encountering the feature during projection.

note.description: Optional human-readable note explaining the behavior (e.g. why an operator is approximated).

input_contract.description: The schema reference (a logical name or $id) governing the adapter's input shape. A non-empty string; resolved against the schema loader at runtime.

output_contract.description: The schema reference (a logical name or $id) governing the adapter's output shape. A non-empty string; resolved against the schema loader at runtime.

deterministic.description: Whether the adapter's output is a pure function of its input (no RNG seed dependence, no wall-clock dependence, no nondeterministic hardware intrinsics). A lossy projection through a non-deterministic adapter is a stronger claim of evidence; the honesty rules in docs/contracts/transformations.md require this to be carried into the receipt.

network_access.description: The adapter's network posture: 'none' (fully offline), 'allowlisted' (calls a fixed, named set of endpoints), or 'required' (cannot run without network). A projection through a network-required adapter cannot be claimed as a closed-form derivation.

license_spdx.description: The SPDX license identifier of the adapter pack (e.g. 'Apache-2.0', 'MIT', 'BSD-3-Clause'). Carried so a downstream agent can refuse a projection whose pack license is incompatible with its policy. NOT a claim that this profile is licensed to run; that is a governance decision.

canonical_writes.description: Safety const: a profile is immutable once authored. Always 0; a non-zero value is a contract violation.

grants_authority.description: Safety const: a profile never grants authority to run its adapter. Always false; a true value is a contract violation. Whether the adapter may run is a governance decision, not a profile property.
